whatItIs: Not a writing-standard repo. vercel/eve is "The Open Framework for Building Agents" — a 5,226-file TypeScript monorepo (`gh api repos/vercel/eve/git/trees/main?recursive=1`). The "Vercel writing standard" inside it is one agent skill: `.agents/skills/technical-writing/`, 365 lines across 8 files (SKILL.md 78, references/{writing-workflow 45, editing-workflow 51, review-framework 49, style-rules 51, prose-quality 47, content-types 40}.md, agents/openai.yaml 4). Scoped to one repository by name: the description field says "for the eve repository", and rules like "Write `eve` lowercase" are hardcoded. Separately, the repo carries three CI scripts that do check documents mechanically — those are not part of the skill and are the only measuring artifacts here.
method: The skill is a verification-first prescription with a routing header. `SKILL.md:10-17` dispatches to one of two workflows (new page vs. edit) plus a mandatory review pass. Its distinctive move is a ranked source hierarchy for truth (`SKILL.md:21-30`): current source/types/tests in `packages/eve` > CLI help > existing docs > merged PRs and release notes > `research/` plans as *proposed intent, not shipped behavior* > Slack/issue evidence, with the explicit instruction "Use support evidence to identify the reader's problem, not to establish product behavior," and for docs-only changes "compare the implementation with the latest public release so the docs do not announce branch-only behavior." Review is five ordered passes (`references/review-framework.md`): purpose/structure, technical accuracy, completeness, style/retrieval, diff discipline — accuracy before style, with "a wrong command, nonexistent API, unsafe instruction, or false guarantee" named a blocker (:21) and "Leave clear, correct prose unchanged" as the closing line (:49). Two reader models run through it: a human doing a task, and a retrieval agent reading one section out of context — hence "Include the critical fact locally because retrieved sections may be read without their links" (`SKILL.md:44`) and "Confirm that each section makes sense when retrieved independently" (`references/writing-workflow.md:45`). `references/prose-quality.md:22-35` lists ten "contextual warning signs" (unsupported importance, promotional language, superficial analysis, vague attribution, stock rhetoric, decorative rhythm, mechanical diction, chatbot artifacts, weak endings, decorative formatting) and prefixes them "Treat these as warnings, not mechanical bans" — then `references/style-rules.md:16` contradicts that with a flat banned-word list (easy, simple, quick, just, obviously, utilize, facilitate, leverage, robust, seamless). `references/content-types.md:3` deliberately declaws Diataxis: the four categories are "structural heuristics, not mandatory frontmatter," and `writing-workflow.md:18` adds "Do not add `contentType` frontmatter solely because this skill categorizes the page."
measures:
The skill measures nothing. It has no answer key, no reader, no score, no failure taxonomy; its one scoring-adjacent line is a prohibition — `references/prose-quality.md:47`: "Do not assign an AI score or claim to know whether AI wrote the text." Prescription, as expected.

The repository around it does measure documents, deterministically, and gates CI on it. `package.json:"docs:check"` = `check-docs.mjs && check-doc-snippets.mjs && check-doc-mdx.mjs`, run in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:44-45` ("Validate /docs/public frontmatter and nav"). What the three actually compute:
- `scripts/check-docs.mjs` (356 lines): required frontmatter fields per root (`title`, `description`, :33); sidebar reachability — every page must be named in an ancestor `meta.json#pages`, covered by a `"..."` wildcard, or on a 1-entry exemption list, else "page would be orphaned from the sidebar" (:183-190); internal-link resolution against the set of actually-rendered URLs, honoring frontmatter `url:` overrides (:197-241); `meta.json` entries resolve to a real file (:243-280); and `checkChannelHubLinks` (:300-325) — the hub page `docs/channels/overview.mdx` must contain a body link to every child route listed in `channels/meta.json`. It prints a count on success: "ok — N files validated."
- `scripts/check-doc-snippets.mjs` (88 lines): extracts every ```ts/tsx/typescript fence under `docs/`, pulls each `eve`/`eve/*` module specifier, and checks it against the set built from `packages/eve/package.json#exports` (:29-33). Its header comment states the selection criterion outright (:8-12): "Full type-checking of every snippet is noisy because many blocks are intentional fragments; validating import specifiers against the exports map is deterministic and catches the highest-frequency failure with no false positives."
- `scripts/check-doc-mdx.mjs` (73 lines): compiles every page with `@mdx-js/mdx` in md or mdx mode by extension, failing on parse errors.
One more, outside `docs:check`: `apps/docs/lib/geistdocs/llms-index.test.ts` is a vitest suite over a hand-written prose document (`llms-index.ts`, the agent-facing entry index) asserting required section headings, a required disambiguation sentence, >20 links, all link URLs unique, and total length < 12,000 characters.

So: structure, links, import paths, syntax, and one byte budget. Nothing measures whether a reader got an answer.

transferable.approach: Doc-vs-code invariant with an explicit zero-false-positive selection rule: extract every code fence's import specifiers and check them against the package's real `exports` map, rather than typechecking snippets.
transferable.whereItLives: scripts/check-doc-snippets.mjs:29-33 (specifier set built from packages/eve/package.json#exports), rationale at :8-12, extraction at :45-69
transferable.whyItMightWork: This is terse's "answer key from the CODE" reduced to the one claim class a machine can settle for free, and the comment states the rule for choosing it: pick the check that is deterministic and catches the highest-frequency failure with no false positives. Cheap pre-pass before the expensive reader seats — a doc whose imports do not exist will produce reader failures that audit would have to classify as lies, one paid model call at a time.
transferable.collidesWith: Nothing in terse. It sits upstream of audit's answer key, not in place of it. Only caution: it is a CI-shaped artifact, and terse ships two skills, not a CI job — it would have to run as a step inside audit, not as a gate.

transferable.approach: Reachability as a measured property of the doc set: compute rendered URLs, then flag any page no other page links to, and require a hub page to body-link every child declared in its nav manifest.
transferable.whereItLives: scripts/check-docs.mjs:183-190 (nav-coverage orphan check), :197-241 (link resolution against the rendered-URL set), :300-325 (checkChannelHubLinks — hub must link every meta.json child)
transferable.whyItMightWork: audit already classifies failures as lie / placement / findability. Findability has no deterministic component today; this supplies one. A page with zero inbound body links is a findability failure that can be proven before any seat reads anything, and the hub-link check is the exact mechanical form of "the page that owns the topic must point at it."
transferable.collidesWith: Partially overlaps audit's findability class — it would pre-empt some findability failures rather than contradict them. Worth knowing before lifting: eve's own skill says the sidebar version of this check is insufficient (SKILL.md:45, "a meta.json sidebar entry or a routing-table cell alone is not enough"), so copy the body-link variant at :300-325, not the nav-coverage variant at :183-190.

transferable.approach: Put the agent-facing entry document under a unit test with a hard byte budget, a uniqueness assertion over its links, and required-section assertions.
transferable.whereItLives: apps/docs/lib/geistdocs/llms-index.test.ts:30-38 (urls.length > 20, new Set(urls).size === urls.length, output.length < 12_000); required sections at :10-17
transferable.whyItMightWork: A cheap, honest ruler for the one document whose reader is a model with a context limit. Duplicate links and unbounded growth are measurable and were measured here. If terse ever emits a revised entry document, this is the shape of test that keeps a later edit from quietly doubling it.
transferable.collidesWith: Brushes against the rejected "hard per-sentence word limits" — but this is a whole-document byte ceiling on one agent-facing index, not a per-sentence rule, and it is asserted in a test rather than enforced by a linter. Different class; still, the distinction has to be stated or it will read as the rejected thing.

transferable.approach: Judge doctrine for a scored bake-off: deterministic assertion first and a judge only when nothing deterministic will do; a three-rung ladder of tracked (no gate) → .atLeast(t) soft → .gate(t) hard; the judge model resolved separately and never the model under test; failure receipts printing prompt, criteria, response, rationale, and choice.

The tracked rung lets a new metric ride along for several runs before it can block anything — which is how a measurement earns the right to gate. "Judge never the model under test" is the same separation audit already gets by using fresh cheap readers, stated as a rule worth writing down.

The one real tension: eve makes judges soft by default and terse's audit score is the gate — terse would be choosing the .gate() rung for its reader score, which the doctrine permits but treats as the exception. Reference-grade, not a drop-in file.

weaknesses:
Four, in order of how much they should cool enthusiasm.

1. The skill is unmeasured by its own lights. 365 lines of rules, 3 commits, about one month old, and not one line of evidence anywhere in the repo that any rule improved a reader's outcome. It is exactly the class already measured and beaten by unguided controls.

2. It contradicts itself on bans. `references/prose-quality.md:24` says "Treat these as warnings, not mechanical bans. Keep an intentional construction when it is the clearest choice"; `references/style-rules.md:16` then bans ten words outright. An agent following both files gets no resolution.

3. Its strongest invariant is prescribed and not enforced. `SKILL.md:45` demands "at least one descriptive inbound body link from a related hub or overview page; a `meta.json` sidebar entry or a routing-table cell alone is not enough ... keep every page reachable by following body links from `getting-started`." What CI actually checks is `meta.json` coverage (`check-docs.mjs:183-190`) — the thing the skill just said is not enough — plus body-link coverage for exactly one folder, `docs/channels/`, via a hardcoded `hubPath` at `check-docs.mjs:301`. So the rule was learned from a real failure (commit c358fa93, "docs: cross-link orphaned pages from hub pages (#2148)", which `gh api repos/vercel/eve/commits/c358fa93` shows touched `SKILL.md` plus 5 doc pages and no script) and then left to prose.

4. A second prescribed-not-measured coupling: `references/content-types.md:29` says "keep `llms-index.ts` in step with the sidebar," and `llms-index.test.ts` never reads `meta.json` — it only asserts section names against the string the same file defines. A self-consistency test, not a drift test.

Also worth stating plainly: the agent-facing docs surface here is substantial (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `agents.md`, `sitemap.md`, `llms.mdx/[[...slug]]` routes under `apps/docs/app/[lang]/`) and the skill names retrieval agents as readers — the same premise as terse's audit — yet nobody ever sends a reader through and counts. The convergence is on the diagnosis; the divergence is that eve stops at prescribing.
